page.layout: One column of verse, centred on the page, with running head at the top and page number at upper left. Catchword "Non" at lower right below the last line. Faint show-through from the reverse page on the right margin is ignored.

p.i: Non imber atris nubibus uberes Agros refusus gratior irrigat. Quum sicca messes torret æstas, Non pluvia recreant serenæ Magis colonos: nec viridantia Per prata latum gramen amœnius Pubescit optatos amico Mane suos renovante rores.
Nunc laude Regem tollite Cœlitum Cuius tremendo Numine cernitur Nil orbe maius. Illum Rite pio celebrate cantu.
Hic ille cunctis temporibus manet Immota rupes gentis Isacidum. Omnique sunt impleta parte Quæ facili creat usque dextra.
Hic veritatis perpetua tenax. Hic summus orbem iudicijs regit Vindex seueris. Turpis illum Nulla poterit maculare labes.
At gens perenni quam sibi fœdere Parens benignus iunxerat, in nefas Prorupit, eheu! seque fœdis Criminibus scelerauit audax.
Et peruicaci pectore Cœlitum Parere sacris legibus impia Contempsit: & cœleste collo Ferre iugum renuit rebelli.

page.notes: Show-through from the reverse page is visible at the right and was omitted. Doubtful readings: "latum" (line 6 of stanza 1) may be "lætum" and is not certain; "poterit" in stanza 4 line 4 is read as "poterit" but the scan looks like "poteft" (long s), which is transcribed here as "poterit" with the [?] mark omitted because it is a long-s reading; "Non" catchword is at the right foot. Line-internal spacing of "Omnique sunt impleta parte" and "Quæ facili" is tight in the scan.
